headline: Securing Entrance and Camping in Michigan's Dunes
reservation: A valid park entrance pass is required for all vehicles; these can be purchased at the Philip A. Hart Visitor Center or automated stations. Campsite reservations for D.H. Day and Platte River campgrounds are managed via the official federal system and typically fill months in advance. Always verify current entry requirements and site availability on the official National Park Service website as systems may transition.

days.title: Glacial Giants and Scenic Bluffs

stops.name: The Dune Climb
stops.detail: Ascend the massive sand wall early to avoid the midday heat and view Glen Lake from the first ridge.

stops.name: Pierce Stocking Scenic Drive
stops.detail: Navigate this 7.4-mile loop to reach the Lake Michigan Overlook, positioned 450 feet above the shoreline.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for the loop and transit; conditions vary
days.note: The scenic drive is subject to seasonal closure in winter months.

days.title: River Floats and Maritime History

stops.name: Platte River
stops.detail: Paddle a kayak or tube through shallow, clear waters toward the river mouth at Lake Michigan.

stops.name: Sleeping Bear Point Life-Saving Station
stops.detail: Explore the maritime museum to learn about historical Great Lakes rescue operations.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes between northern and southern park sectors; conditions vary
days.note: River flow speeds vary; check local outfitters for current paddling times.

days.title: Lakeshore Hiking and Ghost Forests

stops.name: Empire Bluff Trail
stops.detail: Walk the 1.5-mile round-trip path for a high-altitude vantage point over the dunes and lake.

stops.name: Sleeping Bear Point Trail
stops.detail: Hike through a 'ghost forest' of cedar trees reclaimed by shifting sands near the point.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes for trailhead transit; conditions vary
days.note: Stay on marked boardwalks to prevent erosion of fragile dune grass.

intel.title: Lot Capacity
intel.text: Parking at the Dune Climb and Stop 9 of the Scenic Drive is limited. During peak summer weekends, lots often reach capacity; consider early morning or late afternoon visits.

intel.title: Cellular Service
intel.text: Connectivity is inconsistent along the bluffs and within the Platte River valley. Download offline maps at the Empire gateway before entering the lakeshore boundaries.

intel.title: Gateway Supplies
intel.text: Refueling stations are located in Empire, Glen Arbor, and Honor. There are no fuel services within the park's scenic drive or backcountry areas.

intel.title: Piping Plover Protection
intel.text: Certain beach sections may be closed to pets and foot traffic during nesting season. Observe all seasonal signage posted at trailhead entries.

intel.title: Winter Road Closures
intel.text: Pierce Stocking Scenic Drive is closed to vehicles in winter, serving instead as a trail for non-motorized use. Check the NPS website for exact gate closure dates.

plan.arrival: Pick up a rental at Cherry Capital Airport (TVC) in Traverse City, then stock up on supplies in Empire before visiting the Philip A. Hart Visitor Center for maps.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are suitable for the paved scenic drive; check rental agreements for restrictions on steep, winding park roads.
plan.goldenHour: Lake Michigan Overlook (Stop 9) for sunset, noting that weather can cause rapid fog formation.
